name: Nawaru
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: PNG (Yareban); only Ray 1938 comparative survey wordlist material; no grammar or phonology located

sources.citation: Weimer, Harry & Natalia Weimer. 1972. Yareba phonemes. Te Reo 15: 52-57 (and Weimer & Weimer 1975, A short sketch of Yareba grammar, PL C-29: 667-729) -- sister language Yareba (yare1248), not Nawaru.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: For Yareba (closest sister, 'very similar' per Ethnologue): 'Stress is phonemic' (PL C-29 p.670; Te Reo 15 sec.3 p.56). Not a statement about Nawaru; noted only as family context (seen via the catalog store record, not re-read in full here).

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid page and JSON for nawa1258 (Nawaru; alt. name Sirio; Yareban > Yareba-Bariji-Nawaru); only descriptive ref = Weimer 1978; Ray 1938 cited for classification.
Weimer, Harry. 1978 (Aug.). Comparative grammar of five Yareban Family languages. Unpublished SIL-PNG manuscript, 34 pp. SIL Language & Culture Archives item 47691 (= Glottolog ref 48352).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Morphosyntax only (verbs, directionals, pronouns, plurals, clitics, sentences, texts incl. a Sirio text). Conclusion notes only 'significant sound changes and intonation differences' among the five languages and defers to Weimer & Weimer 1975 Yareba sketch for everything else.

sources.citation: Weimer, Harry & Natalia Weimer. 1977 (Feb.). Phoneme comparisons of the Yareban Family. Unpublished SIL-PNG manuscript, 18 pp. SIL Language & Culture Archives item 47692.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No stress rule stated for Sirio (=Nawaru). Sec. 2-3 (pp.2-4, read as page images) treat vowels, diphthongs, consonant inventories ('twelve in Sirio') and contrastive pairs only; the only stress prose (p.5) is about the Oiso dialect of Maria ('a fairly complex system of stress, possible tone.. An attempt will be made, however, to mark stress'). The 140-item comparative word list (pp.6-11) marks stress with an acute on every form in all columns including Sirio: e.g. bebétu 'mouth', ibó 'nose', gorári 'neck', náitai 'eye', desíni 'belly', ófe 'skin', éme 'man', awéta 'woman', kowá 'sun', konúa '…
